What is AI, in 2026?

A system that read almost everything,

then got trained to be useful,

then got handed tools.

Everything else is engineering.

2:30Three beats. (1) Pretraining: predict the next word across the internet, and it turned out that scales into general capability. (2) Post-training: RLHF is what turned a text engine into something that answers you. Without it, no ChatGPT. Reasoning models are the same idea trained on maths and code. (3) Tools: give it functions to call and let it see the result.

If someone asks "isn't it just the 2017 transformer paper?" — the transformer is the engine block. The car is these three layers plus a lot of unglamorous engineering.

What is an AI Agent?

A model, with tools, in a loop.

It doesn't just answer. It does real things.

on your computer

or even stuff plugged into it.

How does it differ from a chat bot?

Builders, editors, CLI agents, code review bots, QA agents, always-on agents, orchestrators — new ones every week. Nobody is expected to know all of these, including me.

Point: this is the landscape, and it's genuinely too much to track. That's normal. Pick one and go deep rather than chasing all of them.

Remote work untethered families from cities.

AI is untethering work itself.

It's why this community exists. It's also why this talk does.

6:00The Revillage pitch is that remote work made living anywhere possible. That's the last untethering. This one changes what a day of work is. Not "adapt or die" — more that the people who understand this early get to choose how it shows up in their family.

What do we want for our kids?

Ban it?

Three prompts

Something AI did this month that surprised you

Something you refuse to let AI do for you

A recurring annoyance you'd hand off tomorrow

7:30Pairs or threes, five minutes each prompt, then a couple of shares back to the room. The first two work at any skill level. The third one is the project harvest: stickies on the wall. Work stuff or village stuff — meals for eighteen, the kid rota, French bureaucracy.
